subject: Audit stream exportability and tamper-evidence guarantees (RFI)
messages:
From: Alexi Petrov <procurement@everbank.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: RFI: Audit stream exportability and tamper-evidence guarantees

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the helpful webinar last week — Everbank is evaluating Redwood for a production deployment and we need to validate exportability and forensic guarantees for audit logs as part of our RFP. Could you please provide concise answers to the questions below (we'll follow up with your security contact if needed):

1) Retention windows: What default retention windows do you offer for audit logs and user activity traces? Can customers configure shorter/longer retention per-account?

2) Export formats & fidelity: Which export formats are supported for bulk audit extracts (CSV, NDJSON, Parquet)? Are token-level metadata, PK/trace identifiers, and KV cache events included? Any limits on record size?

3) Export delivery & SLA: How are exports delivered (S3 presigned, SFTP, direct push)? SLA for bulk export job completion for a 30-day extract of 50M events?

4) Tamper evidence & chain of custody: What mechanisms are used to provide tamper-evidence (append-only storage, digest manifests, signed manifests, HSM-wrapped keys)? Can you provide a sample manifest layout?

5) Legal preservation & forensics: For legal hold requests, can Redwood take immutable snapshots and provide a signed bundle with provenance metadata (timestamps, internal job IDs, operator IDs)?

6) Partial/filtered extracts: Can exports be sliced by time range, user id, route/model id, or request-id? Are filters guaranteed to be consistent (no missing records) if applied across partitions?

7) Encryption / Key control: Is exported data encrypted at rest and in transit? Can customers use their own KMS keys for exports?

We'd appreciate a short matrix response and any sample artifacts you can attach. If possible, please keep the initial answer to a single page; we'll request a deeper playbook after the procurement review.

Best,
Alexi
Alexi Petrov
Senior Sourcing Analyst — Everbank
procurement@everbank.com

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T11:03:00-05:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Audit stream exportability and tamper-evidence guarantees

Alexi — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a short export spec and an example NDJSON extract plus a digest manifest for illustration. Happy to expand any line item.

1) Retention windows:
- Default audit log retention (hosted): 90 days for high-cardinality request traces, 365 days for summary-level events.
- Custom retention: Customers can configure retention per-account down to 7 days, or to indefinite (multi-year) for Dedicated/Private deployments via policy.

2) Export formats & fidelity:
- Supported formats: NDJSON (preferred for line-delimited events), Parquet for columnar analytics, CSV for simple tables.
- Included fields: timestamp (RFC3339 UTC), request_id, user_id (if present), route/model_id, token_count, request_payload_hash, response_hash, KV-cache indicators, operator/admin actions, error codes, and internal job_ids.
- Limits: Individual event payloads are limited to 1MB; large payloads are chunked with a chunk_id and sequence number.

3) Export delivery & SLA:
- Delivery methods: S3 presigned URLs (preferred), SFTP push, Azure Blob SAS, or direct HTTPS POST to a customer endpoint.
- SLA: For Hosted exports, a 30-day extract of 50M events is targeted for completion within 8 hours (standard), 4 hours for Dedicated with priority SLAs.

4) Tamper evidence & chain of custody:
- Mechanisms: Append-only internal ledger for audit writes; export-stage manifest generation signed with an HSM-backed key; SHA-256 per-record digests plus a top-level Merkle root in the manifest.
- Operator metadata: manifest includes job_id, operator_id (redacted per policy if needed), start/end timestamps, export filters, and export checksum per file.
- Sample manifest: attached as redwood_export_digest_manifest.txt (see attachment).

5) Legal preservation & forensics:
- Snapshots: We support immutable snapshotting for legal hold (bit-for-bit export). Snapshots are packaged with the manifest and a provenance file which lists internal replication IDs and node checksums.
- Signing: Snapshots are signed using an HSM-protected key. We can provide certificate chains upon NDA.

6) Partial/filtered extracts:
- Filtering: Supported by time range, user_id, request_id, route/model_id, region, and tag keys.
- Consistency guarantee: Exports run with a snapshot-consistent view. When filters are applied, the system ensures no cross-partition gaps for the requested interval; manifests include expected record counts per shard to validate completeness.

7) Encryption / Key control:
- Encryption: All exports are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and at rest. Export files placed in customer S3 are encrypted server-side; for additional control we support client-side encryption and customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK).

Attachments included in this reply:
- everbank_audit_export_spec.xlsx (spreadsheet with field mapping and example queries)
- redwood_log_export_example.ndjson (50 lines sample)
- redwood_export_digest_manifest.txt (sample manifest with SHA-256 per-file and Merkle root)

If this matches what you need I can loop in our security engineering team for the deeper artifact set (cert chains, HSM vendor details) and propose a delivery SLA for the POC.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Trust & Safety Engineer — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

Mina — thanks for the quick summary and the sample artifacts. A couple of clarifying questions from our security team before we loop legal: 

1) HSM & signing: Do you use a single global HSM per region or can keys be provisioned per-customer in Dedicated/Private? Will you share the signing certificate fingerprint?
2) Manifest retention: How long do you keep the signed manifests and can they be retained separately from the underlying event data?
3) Snapshot reproducibility: If we request the same snapshot twice (same filter set & job_id) will you reproduce identical files and manifest checksums; or do manifests include transient metadata that changes on each run?

Also — may we schedule a 30-minute technical call with your security engineering team? Proposed slots: 2026-12-07 10:00-12:00 ET or 2026-12-08 14:00-15:00 ET.

Regards,

Thanks — quick answers inline and happy to confirm a call. Proposed time: 2026-12-07 10:30 ET (we can do 10:00 if you prefer).

1) HSM & signing: For Hosted, we manage HSMs per-region (AWS CloudHSM). For Dedicated and Private deployments we can provision a dedicated HSM per-customer and import customer keys (subject to legal/operational onboarding). We will share the certificate fingerprint under an NDA; operational fingerprints are also embedded in the manifest signature section.

2) Manifest retention: Signed manifests are retained for the life of the export retention policy by default. We can configure separate retention for manifests (e.g., retain manifests for 7 years while event data is 1 year) for Dedicated/Private customers.

3) Snapshot reproducibility: Exports are snapshot-based and deterministic for the given filter/job_id pair. Manifests include an export_generation_id and node-level checksums; repeating the same snapshot run with identical parameters will produce identical file-level checksums and Merkle root. Transient metadata (e.g., job submission timestamp) is normalized in the manifest to ensure reproducibility if requested.

Action items:
- I'll send a calendar invite for 2026-12-07 10:30 ET and include our security engineer, Kimberly Park, and Marcus for export-engine details.
- I'll also provide a short product note on how to validate a manifest (sha256sum process + Merkle verification steps).

Regards,
Mina
